project.description: The single maven reactor build of the pic-sure monorepo. Every image job consumes this job's per-stack workspace; no other job runs Maven against the monorepo. Fail-closed per module: each built module's build-info/ stamp is removed before maven and rewritten only on success, so an image job can tell whether ITS module was rebuilt rather than trusting one lane-wide file. Builds are serialized (concurrentBuild=false) because the per-stack workspace is shared and concurrent same-stack runs corrupt it; orchestrated runs additionally hold lock(stack-<stack>). Do not run manually while a pipeline holds that stack's lock.

hudson.model.StringParameterDefinition.name: MODULES
hudson.model.StringParameterDefinition.description: Optional comma-separated reactor module paths to build (with -am for upstream deps), e.g. services/pic-sure-logging. Empty builds the full monorepo.

hudson.tasks.Shell.command:
#!/bin/bash set -euo pipefail
: "${TARGET_STACK:?TARGET_STACK is required}"
GIT_BRANCH_SHORT=$(echo "${GIT_BRANCH}" | awk -F/ '{print $NF}') GIT_COMMIT_SHORT=$(echo "${GIT_COMMIT}" | cut -c1-7)
# Fail closed: image jobs must not consume a mixed lane after a failed build. rm -f build-info.txt
# Which modules this run is responsible for stamping. A targeted run owns exactly the # modules it was asked to build; -am also rebuilds their upstream deps, but no image job # reads those, so they need no stamp. A full run owns every reactor module. STAMP_DIR="build-info" mkdir -p "$STAMP_DIR" stamp_modules=() if [ -n "${MODULES:-}" ]; then IFS=',' read -r -a raw_modules <<< "$MODULES" for m in "${raw_modules[@]}"; do m="$(echo "$m" | tr -d '[:space:]')" if [ -n "$m" ]; then stamp_modules+=("$m"); fi done else while IFS= read -r m; do stamp_modules+=("$m"); done \ < <(find . -mindepth 2 -name pom.xml | sed 's|/pom.xml$||; s|^\./||' | sort -u) fi
if [ "${#stamp_modules[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then echo "ERROR: resolved no modules to stamp (MODULES='${MODULES:-}'); image jobs would all fail closed" >&2 exit 1 fi
stamp_path() { echo "$STAMP_DIR/$(printf '%s' "$1" | tr '/' '_').txt"; }
# Fail closed per module: drop the stamp for everything this run rebuilds and rewrite it # only on success. A module outside the selection keeps the stamp describing the jar still # sitting in its target/, which is the whole point of stamping per module. for m in "${stamp_modules[@]}"; do rm -f "$(stamp_path "$m")" done
# Optional targeted build: when MODULES is set, build only those reactor modules # (plus their upstream deps via -am) instead of the full monorepo. Empty = full # build, so the full Pipeline jobs (which pass no MODULES) are unchanged. MVN_GOALS="-B clean install -T1C -DskipTests" if [ -n "${MODULES:-}" ]; then MVN_GOALS="$MVN_GOALS -pl ${MODULES} -am" fi echo "mvn goals: $MVN_GOALS"
# The reactor build for this stack's lane. Identity-map mount (BDC: # host path == container path); per-stack m2 avoids concurrent-install races. docker run --rm \ -v "/var/jenkins_home/workspace/PIC-SURE Maven Build - ${TARGET_STACK}/:/app:z" \ -v "maven_m2_cache_${TARGET_STACK}:/root/.m2" \ -w /app \ --platform=linux/amd64 \ maven:3-amazoncorretto-25 \ sh -lc "mvn $MVN_GOALS"
# Lane-wide copy, kept for this job's console output only. Image jobs read the per-module # stamps below; a lane-wide file cannot tell them whether THEIR module was rebuilt. { echo "GIT_BRANCH_SHORT=$GIT_BRANCH_SHORT" echo "GIT_COMMIT_SHORT=$GIT_COMMIT_SHORT" } > build-info.txt cat build-info.txt
# Tag metadata the image jobs source, one file per module this run actually built. for m in "${stamp_modules[@]}"; do { echo "GIT_BRANCH_SHORT=$GIT_BRANCH_SHORT" echo "GIT_COMMIT_SHORT=$GIT_COMMIT_SHORT" } > "$(stamp_path "$m")" done echo "stamped ${#stamp_modules[@]} module(s) at ${GIT_COMMIT_SHORT}:" printf ' %s\n' "${stamp_modules[@]}"
